Removes noisy, meaningless IWYU output for code that is maintained upstream

result.summary: This PR modifies the IWYU CI step in ci/test/03_test_script.sh to filter out subtree files (using SHARED_EXCLUDED_SUBTREES from the lint config) from compile_commands.json before running IWYU, and adds cleanup logic to revert any subtree header edits IWYU still makes via associated-file heuristics. This stops the non-enforced IWYU pass from analyzing and then reverting changes to libmultiprocess, the only subtree not already excluded via EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS OFF.
result.problem: The IWYU CI job currently prints and then discards IWYU suggestions for 14 libmultiprocess files every run, since libmultiprocess has its own upstream IWYU CI with different versions and mappings that already passes. This wastes CI log space and confuses contributors reading IWYU output, as raised in the closed issue #35361.

resolved_concerns: hebasto asked why not use the cmake-based approach from #35418's review; ryanofsky explained why script-level filtering is preferable (works for all subtrees, doesn't disable clang-tidy/bitcoin-tidy on subtrees, avoids the -DBUILD_TESTS=OFF breakage from #35418/#35523) with no further objection.

result.card: This PR changes ci/test/03_test_script.sh to filter subtree files (via SHARED_EXCLUDED_SUBTREES) out of compile_commands.json before running IWYU in CI, and adds cleanup for any subtree header edits IWYU makes anyway. It solves recurring CI noise where IWYU analyzes and reverts suggestions for the libmultiprocess subtree, whose own upstream CI already runs a different IWYU version and passes, as described in the closed issue #35361.
